C01.name: Cordon
C01.meaning: A cordon is a protective line of guards or barriers enclosing an area, from French "cordon" (cord/ribbon).
C01.clashes: Cordon (by Codezero), a 2026 free tool securing credentials across AI coding agents; Cordon AI (cordon-ai.com), an AI-native multi-model security validation platform; a separate "Cordon" security proxy enforcing policy/audit for AI agent-to-MCP tool calls; CORDONIQ (video conferencing security).
C01.associations: "Cordon sanitaire": a barrier against disease or a political metaphor for isolating a party; mildly exclusionary connotation.

C02.name: Gnomon
C02.meaning: A gnomon is the raised part of a sundial that casts the shadow indicating time (also an L-shaped figure in geometry).
C02.clashes: Gnomon School of Visual Effects, a well-known VFX/games college in North Hollywood; Gnomon Digital, an AI/MLOps consultancy with clients incl. Société Générale and AXA; open-source "Gnomon" guardrails tool for AI coding agents; Gnomon-MCP, a maths/date tool for AI models.
C02.associations: The sundial meaning is obscure to most; overlaps with an established, unrelated VFX education brand.

C03.name: Certes
C03.meaning: Archaic English adverb meaning "certainly, in truth", from Old French, ultimately Latin "certus".
C03.clashes: Certes Networks, a Pittsburgh network-encryption/data-protection company (founded 2000) serving US federal and defence agencies, rebranded as Certes.ai for cybersecurity and data protection.
C03.associations: Archaic word largely unknown in modern English; risk of mispronunciation or being read as a coined word.

C04.name: Hadrian Labs
C04.meaning: Named for Hadrian, Roman emperor (117-138 AD), best known for Hadrian's Wall across northern Britain.
C04.clashes: Hadrian (hadrian.io), an Amsterdam-founded (2021) agentic-AI offensive-security and attack-surface-management platform, recognised by Gartner and GigaOm, well funded and an active competitor in AI security.
C04.associations: Hadrian's Wall (a barrier) and Roman imperial conquest; close overlap with the security company above.

C05.name: Billet Labs
C05.meaning: A billet is lodging assigned to a soldier, or a bar of metal ("machined from billet"); the latter is the common current usage.
C05.clashes: Billet Labs (billetlabs.com), an existing London company (founded 2022, Companies House 14310095) making CNC-machined PC-cooling hardware; a direct UK name clash in a different industry.
C05.associations: "Billet" is everyday jargon in machining, car tuning and PC modding, so the name reads as hardware.

C06.name: AegisVector
C06.meaning: "Aegis" (the protective shield of Zeus/Athena; protection, sponsorship) plus "vector" (direction, carrier; also "attack vector").
C06.clashes: "Project Aegis Vector", a niche GitHub testbed for LLM/RAG vulnerabilities (not a company); otherwise shares the crowded Aegis namespace.
C06.associations: "Attack vector" is security jargon; the compound can read as a generic, machine-generated brand.

C07.name: NovaPulse AI Solutions
C07.meaning: A generic compound of "nova" and "pulse" with no specific meaning.
C07.clashes: Many small firms: Novapulse AI (business intelligence), NovaPulse Labs (cloud engineering), Nova Pulse LLC (SMS marketing), NovaPulse Solutions (SEO), NovaPulse Care (AI voicemail), Novapulse Dynamics (AI content).
C07.associations: Saturated naming pattern; very low distinctiveness.

C08.name: Aegis
C08.meaning: In Greek myth the aegis is the protective shield of Zeus or Athena; hence "under the aegis of".
C08.clashes: Lockheed Martin Aegis Combat System (major US Navy missile-defence brand); AegisAI (aegisai.ai), agentic email-security startup by ex-Google security leads, $36M raised in 2026; Aegis Defence Services, a British private military/security company; many other security products.
C08.associations: Extremely crowded in security and defence branding; strong military association.

C09.name: Sovereign Air
C09.meaning: "Sovereign": supreme, independent authority (cf. data sovereignty); "air": atmosphere or aviation. The proposer's "air gap" link is not a standard usage.
C09.clashes: Sovereign Air LLC, an Orlando private-jet charter operator; Cessna Citation Sovereign business jet; Sovereign Aerospace, a US aircraft company.
C09.associations: Reads as private aviation rather than technology; "sovereign" is heavily used in fintech/govtech.

C10.name: Sentinel
C10.meaning: A sentinel is a soldier or guard stationed to keep watch.
C10.clashes: Microsoft Sentinel (major cloud SIEM, Gartner Leader); SentinelOne (large listed AI-driven cybersecurity company, 10,000+ customers); Thales Sentinel licensing/DRM products; many further security tools.
C10.associations: Extremely overused in security software; also the robot villains in Marvel's X-Men.

C11.name: Cautia
C11.meaning: Not a standard word; nearest roots are Latin "cautio" (a legal guarantee or bond in Roman law) and "cautus" (cautious).
C11.clashes: No company found with this spelling; the near-identical Cautio (Bengaluru) is an AI dashcam and fleet-safety startup with $3M seed funding.

C12.name: Veto Labs
C12.meaning: "Veto" is Latin for "I forbid": the power to block an action unilaterally.
C12.clashes: veto.so, "Stop risky AI actions before they happen", runtime authorisation for AI agents, closely matching this thesis; Ona's "Veto", a kernel-level enforcement engine for AI-agent security (Ona, formerly Gitpod, is a funded dev-tools company); VetoAI, an AI legal drafting tool (India); Veto Technologies, privacy communications devices.
C12.associations: Widely used in politics (UN Security Council veto); short and easy to say.

C13.name: Corbel
C13.meaning: An architectural bracket projecting from a wall to bear weight, from Old French for "crow".
C13.clashes: Corbel (corbelpay.com), AI CPQ/sales platform, $6.7M seed 2026; Corbel AI (usecorbel.tech), stops AI coding agents from breaking production; Corbel Ops, AI operations consulting.
C13.associations: Corbel is also a well-known Microsoft typeface shipped with Windows and Office since 2004.

C14.name: Vouchsafe Labs
C14.meaning: Archaic verb "to vouchsafe": to grant or give something graciously or condescendingly, not "safely vouch for".
C14.clashes: Vouchsafe (vouchsafe.id), UK biometric identity-verification startup, £1m pre-seed 2025; Vouched (vouched.id), US AI identity verification, $17M Series A; open-source "Vouchsafe" identity token standard.
C14.associations: Old-fashioned and formal; a bit hard to say quickly.

C15.name: Countermand Labs
C15.meaning: "To countermand": to cancel an order by issuing a contrary one.
C15.clashes: None found under this name. Nearby but unrelated: Counter Labs (restaurant software), CounterLabs.ai (placeholder), Counter Lab (Duke research group).

C16.name: Imprimatur Labs
C16.meaning: Latin "let it be printed": a Catholic bishop's official permission to publish; by extension, official sanction.
C16.clashes: None found as "Imprimatur Labs". Imprimatur Group (imprimatur.co.uk), 30-year UK automotive translation firm with an AI translation product; Imprimatur Capital Ltd, venture capital.

C17.name: Seneschal
C17.meaning: The chief steward of a medieval royal or noble household, overseeing administration and justice.
C17.clashes: Seneschal Incorporated / Seneschal Consulting, small US management/IT consultancies; Seneschal Voicebot, a small open-source AI voice-agent project; no major AI/security firm.

C18.name: Redoubt
C18.meaning: A small enclosed defensive fortification or place of retreat, often outside a larger fort.
C18.clashes: Redoubt (redoubt.dk), small Copenhagen cybersecurity/backup startup for Shopify stores; Redoubt Networks / Redoubt Solutions, small US IT firms; an open-source RISC-V security OS project.
C18.associations: "American Redoubt" is a survivalist, far-right-associated relocation movement in the US north-west.

C19.name: Auctra
C19.meaning: Not a dictionary word; an invented name echoing Latin auctor/auctoritas (author, authority) or "auction".
C19.clashes: Auctra (auctra.io), real-time spend authorisation for AI agents, closely matching this thesis; Auctra (auctralabs.ai), AI-agent governance layer; Auctra (getauctra.com), AI content verification; Auctra.ai, AI lead qualification for insurance.
C19.associations: Used by at least three AI startups; easily misheard as "auction".

C20.name: VeritasGate Labs
C20.meaning: Invented compound of Latin veritas (truth) and "gate".
C20.clashes: Veritas Technologies, a large, well-known enterprise data-backup/protection company; Veritas Labs Inc., US healthcare AI/staffing; several "Veritas Lab" DNA and drug-testing labs.
C20.associations: "Veritas" is heavily used in enterprise software, mottos, law and forensic testing; "-gate" also suggests scandal.

C21.name: Chancery
C21.meaning: The office or court of the Lord Chancellor; historically England's court of equity.
C21.clashes: Chancery AI Limited (chancery.ai), UK legal-AI startup for law firms, incorporated January 2026; Chancery Software, US education administration software; an open-source "Chancery" AI-agent knowledge-base project.
C21.associations: "In chancery" means trapped in a hopeless position; evokes slow Victorian litigation (Bleak House).

C22.name: Bailiwick Labs
C22.meaning: A bailiwick is the district or jurisdiction of a bailiff; by extension, one's area of authority.
C22.clashes: Bailiwick (bailiwick.com), a Fortune 500 managed IT/site-services provider; Bailiwick Ventures, digital-transformation consulting; Bailiwick VIBE, an AI venture studio. No "Bailiwick Labs" found.
C22.associations: Best known as the Bailiwicks of Jersey and Guernsey, associated with offshore finance.

C23.name: Penstock Labs
C23.meaning: A penstock is a sluice, gate or pipe controlling water flow, e.g. to a hydroelectric turbine.
C23.clashes: Penstock Group (penstockgroup.com), healthcare payment-integrity SaaS, Inc. 5000 #353 in 2025; Pentera, a well-funded pen-testing platform (similar sound); Penstock Coffee Roasters. No "Penstock Labs" found.

C24.name: Claustra Labs
C24.meaning: Latin "claustra": bar, bolt, lock or enclosure (root of "cloister" and "claustrophobia").
C24.clashes: None found in AI, security or software.
C24.associations: In French, a claustra is a perforated screen wall (building materials); root of "claustrophobia".

C25.name: Runnymede Labs
C25.meaning: Runnymede is the Thames-side meadow in Surrey where King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215.
C25.clashes: The Runnymede Corporation (US commercial real estate); Runnymede Borough Council; the Runnymede Trust (a prominent UK race-equality think tank). No "Runnymede Labs" tech company found.
C25.associations: Magna Carta and the rule of law; the name of a UK council and a well-known charity.

C26.name: Chary Labs
C26.clashes: None found in AI or software. Chary.nl (Dutch e-commerce marketing agency); Chary Law (US law firm).
C26.associations: Uncommon word; risk of mispronunciation or misreading as "charity".

C27.name: Anchorite Labs
C27.meaning: An anchorite is a religious hermit, historically sealed into a cell attached to a church.
C27.clashes: Anchorite Labs LLC (Washington State, registered, listed delinquent/inactive); Anchorite Foundation (US non-profit for AI/robotics education). No active AI company.
C27.associations: Monastic, reclusive connotation; may read as obscure or antisocial.

C28.name: Barbican
C28.meaning: A fortified gateway or outer tower guarding the entrance to a castle or walled city.
C28.clashes: Barbican Centre, London, Europe's largest multi-arts venue (large well-known brand); Barbican, an AI-driven SIEM/SOAR security startup; the Barbican Estate, London.
C28.associations: Dominated by London's Barbican Centre and Estate.

C29.name: Seneschal Labs
C29.meaning: A seneschal was a medieval steward who ran a lord's household, estate administration and justice.
C29.clashes: Only small open-source projects (a voice-bot and an AI workflow engine on GitHub) and a small Dubai tenancy platform. No major company.
C29.associations: Archaic, hard to spell and say; common in fantasy fiction and role-playing games.

C30.name: Provost Labs
C30.meaning: A provost is a senior official: head of a university, a Scottish burgh's chief magistrate, or a military-police officer.
C30.clashes: Provost Companies Inc (US landscaping); university "Office of the Provost" AI initiatives. No "Provost Labs" tech company found.
C30.associations: Strongly associated with university administration; may read as institutional.

C31.name: Vallum Labs
C31.meaning: Latin "vallum": a rampart or palisade, as in the earthwork beside Hadrian's Wall.
C31.clashes: Vallum (vallum.ai), an enterprise AI-governance and security platform founded by Stanford/Princeton researchers; Vallum (GitHub), an open-source security proxy for AI coding agents; Vallum Associates, UK tech recruitment; Vallum Software, network management.
C31.associations: Crowded in the adjacent AI-security space.
